summary.prose: Decide whether accepted review work is complete, then publish one canonical code-review record linked to its exact subject and coverage checkpoint. Missing evidence, conflicting requirements, stale source and a non-independent reviewer prevent publication. Publication is recoverable after interruption and preserves the existing verdict and human approval rules.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: a daemon-owned durable investigation state machine with provider-independent accepted state. Seed each run with sc1's approved tasks/checks, artifact references and explicit commit packets, not embedded source partitions. Source-only and indexed-impact runs use identical packets, obligations, reviewer policy and completion checks; only the indexed capability in sc3 differs. Substantive judgments remain the independent agent's job; deterministic guards validate identity, evidence provenance, coverage and publication, not semantic correctness. Reuse existing LLMProvider/CliProvider read-only execution, budget admission, source freshness, ownership and canonical artifact lifecycle; introduce the investigation protocol and durable accepted-state store behind the existing code-review entrypoints. Checkpoint cadence is per reviewed commit-packet block, independently of continuation boundaries and run time limits; multiple block checkpoints may be accepted within one managed reviewer session.

ownedContracts.name: ReviewCompletionV1
ownedContracts.purpose: Validate accountable coverage and source applicability before one canonical CR publication. Required unverified work blocks successful completion; findings retain existing severity/confidence and human override policy.

consumedContracts.name: ImmutableReviewSubjectV1
consumedContracts.purpose: The only authority for changed scope. Exact selected commit packets identify relevant parent-relative blocks; frozen context can include other source only as context. No HEAD/working-tree diff fallback.

consumedContracts.name: EvidenceCoverageV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Run-scoped evidence and many-to-many coverage bindings. Each approved obligation, packet block/non-text change and applicable criterion has a required row; findings and unresolved work cannot disappear.

consumedContracts.name: InvestigationContinuationV1
consumedContracts.purpose: One bounded independent read-only investigation protocol for both entrypoints/modes. Provider sessions execute requests but never own scope, accepted coverage or completion. Accept incremental per-block progress and durable acknowledgments inside one managed continuation; final replies reference accepted block receipts. Domain protocol only; s6 owns external MCP registration. Legacy sibling 8315a11f/S005 sc7 remains separate.

consumedContracts.name: DurableReviewRecoveryV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Daemon-owned acceptance journal, reconstructible checkpoints and exclusive generation/lease fencing; accepted replies are idempotent, uncertain provider outcomes remain explicit. Checkpoint per reviewed block, not only after a whole provider request or at the run time limit.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewRuntimePortsV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Foundational type-level ports avoid making the investigation Story depend backwards on recovery. s4 implements durable storage, s3 uses the port, and s6 composes production adapters. Usage observations flow to existing usage contracts with a durable pending outbox when a writer is unavailable.

boundary.internal: Own completion coverage/freshness/party validation, canonical CR adaptation and idempotent terminal publication receipts. Reuse existing lifecycle and severity/confidence policy. Do not let a completion request, missing evidence or a failed run masquerade as a completed verdict.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own subject preparation, attribution ambiguity detection, exact Git commit/blob/block navigation and frozen context binding. Define foundational runtime-port types only; do not implement task investigation, a recovery store or new accounting storage. No generic HEAD/working-tree diff may select scope.

Own required-row enumeration, evidence identity/provenance and coverage relationships/dispositions. Reuse subject inputs and runtime ports. Keep ledger validation helpers private; do not execute reviewer turns or publish CRs.

Own independent read-only task-directed continuation behavior, on-demand source navigation, optional indexed caller/impact enrichment, budget admission, bounded retry/pause and attempt usage emission through foundational ports. In-memory ports are test scaffolding while production selection remains disabled until s4/s6; no durable storage implementation or terminal approval logic. Publish and acknowledge incremental block progress within continuations, with partial cross-block assessments recorded rather than lost. Domain progress contracts only; no competing MCP phase/schema ownership. External registration belongs to s6.

Own durable implementation of foundational acceptance/usage-outbox ports, append/replay/checkpoint integrity, lease/generation fencing, uncertain attempts and compatibility/time recovery. Do not alter review criteria or introduce a usage warehouse. Its recovery implementation is composed by downstream s6 rather than consumed backwards by s3. Persist/replay block-level evidence and assessment receipts independently of final provider-call completion.

Own production composition, equivalent MCP/daemon/controller start/status/resume/cancel adapters, status/usage presentation fields, explicit engine rollout/rollback, legacy compatibility and evaluation fixtures. No client opens stores directly; no client-specific board UI or design-review replacement. Sole new-engine MCP adapter/schema owner; reconcile 8315a11f/S005 legacy sc7 as specified in the architecture and record code-only supersession before opt-in. Verify routing partitions across both installation orders.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: E — complete and publish one canonical review

nonFunctional.performance: No eager whole-source or whole-contract repetition and no mandatory call-per-clause. Bounded read ranges and explicit evidence references prevent unbounded request growth.128K inclusive estimated admission and five-minute continuation cap; default120active-minute/24continuation limits pause with durable progress and explicit extension rather than claim success. Use deterministic/mock providers for routine tests; measure authorized live comparisons against recorded baselines before claiming savings. Block checkpoint acceptance is independent of run duration:120minutes is a pause ceiling, never a save interval. Grouping several block assessments in one session remains allowed.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns runtime state and DB access; cloud access remains LLMProvider/CliProvider only. Independent reviewer identity is checked at start and publication. Source reads are pinned and read-only; untrusted repository text is data, not tool/policy authority. Trusted evidence reads cannot escape the declared snapshot/approved-artifact view, graph queries bind to the registered source repo and declared dependency closure, and native adapters that cannot meet pinning/read-only capability refuse explicitly. Private runtime state uses restrictive access; metadata diagnostics contain no raw prompts/evidence.
nonFunctional.observability: Expose run/subject/engine/policy IDs, owner generation, attempt lifecycle, required/covered/unverified rows, pause/stale causes and resume compatibility. Show managed attempt count/active time, observed usage quality and unknown/pending observations distinctly from reservations and estimates. Emit status/heartbeats without replaying accepted work; transport disconnect is not a review verdict. Keep human-readable review reports only in /tmp. Surface latest accepted block/progress receipt and outstanding block IDs so clients can distinguish durable block progress from provider-session liveness.
nonFunctional.durability: Journal-committed acceptance precedes acknowledgment; snapshots/checkpoints are reconstructible and verified against immutable evidence/answer blobs. Detect torn tails and corruption, fence concurrent owners and late replies, preserve uncertain provider outcomes and idempotent completion/usage receipts. Pauses do not erase consumed execution time. Legacy runs are explicitly non-resumable; runtime data remains outside artifact JSON and excluded from changed scope. Every reviewed block is journal-committed before its durable acknowledgment and cursor advancement, even while a native session continues. Accepted block state survives an uncertain or failed enclosing attempt; only unfinished/unacknowledged work is resumed.

api.name: CompletionAssessmentV1
api.signature: interface CompletionAssessmentV1 { readonly runId: string; readonly subjectDigest: string; readonly checkpointDigest: string; readonly outcome: 'publishable' | 'incomplete' | 'stale' | 'conflict'; readonly unresolvedRows: readonly string[]; readonly reasons: readonly string[]; readonly requiredCriteria: readonly string[]; }

returns.meaning: Deterministic assessment of an immutable accepted checkpoint, not a review verdict or human approval.

errors.condition: Corrupt, unsupported or foreign recovery state; ownership lost.

preconditions: Trusted daemon supplies current registered repo, approved BUILD/contract pins, independent party records and replayed sc4 state.
No issued/partially-accepted attempt remains active; uncertain/failed enclosing attempts may retain accepted blocks but cannot themselves certify completion.
postconditions: Every required task, acceptance, design, change, criterion and applicable impact row has an explicit validated disposition.
Pending or unverified required rows, outstanding work and unfinished selected blocks produce incomplete; conflicts remain for human resolution; freshness mismatch produces stale.

api.name: ReviewCompletionReceiptV1
api.signature: interface ReviewCompletionReceiptV1 { readonly receiptId: string; readonly runId: string; readonly subjectDigest: string; readonly terminalCheckpointDigest: string; readonly artifactId: string; readonly artifactRevision: number; readonly verdict: 'pass' | 'warn' | 'block'; readonly coverageRef: string; }

returns.meaning: Verified canonical CR identity/revision and durable accepted coverage link, emitted only after canonical persistence is confirmed.

errors.condition: Completion not publishable, stale pins, publication intent conflict, ownership loss or uncertain canonical write.

preconditions: Assessment remains publishable at the frozen checkpoint and immediately before canonical CAS.
sc4 prerequisite provides durable frozen intent, owner-fenced publication and completion-requested lease recovery; not supplied by s5 private-event writes.
postconditions: One operation identity maps to one canonical revision; identical replay returns original receipt and does not invoke judges or append another revision.
Human BUILD approval and override remain separate actions; completed block/warn CR is distinct from incomplete execution.

api.name: RecoveryStore
api.signature: class RecoveryStore { requestCompletion(leaseId: string, generation: number): Promise<RecoveryView>; recordCompletion(leaseId: string, generation: number, receipt: string): Promise<RecoveryView>; }

returns.meaning: Consumed existing sc4 transition/receipt boundary; exact inherited types remain unchanged.

errors.condition: Stale owner, conflicting terminal receipt or unsupported recovery.

preconditions: Consume only sc4 public capabilities; do not author its private event envelopes.
postconditions: Only sc4 owns run-state journal and fencing. sc5 owns eligibility and canonical adaptation.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed new files: src/workflow/code-review/investigation/completion-types.ts defines exact sc5 types and typed completion errors; src/workflow/code-review/investigation/completion-assessment.ts evaluates one replayed immutable checkpoint. Consume validateReviewLedger and trusted receipt closure. Enumerate required criteria from basis, never reviewer-selected subset; verify exact required row universe and all selected packet/non-text blocks have latest accepted disposition reviewed, with no retained follow-up/outstanding work. Valid findings remain accountable dispositions and can yield a completed blocking verdict. Satisfaction/not-applicable still require sc2 evidence/applicability checks. A requirement marked finding is accountable only if its linked evidence and finding references validate. Changes absent from PLAN remain required change rows and must be independently judged, never silently dropped. Conflicts between approved expectations are supplied as trusted unresolved contract-decision references or evidence-linked reviewer conflicts and return conflict; do not derive semantic contradictions from string matching or silently rewrite expectations. Evidence-scoped unavailable/partial records cannot support a stronger disposition than sc2 permits. Unknown party or same author/reviewer is conflict; re-read canonical BUILD authorPartyOf and authenticated review party, not model-supplied labels. [c1,c2,c3]

Proposed new file: src/workflow/code-review/investigation/completion-publication.ts builds/stages an immutable intent containing version, deterministic operationId, run/subject/policy/checkpoint digests, coverageRef and coverage digest, candidate CR content digest, canonical CR id, expected prior revision or explicit absent state, pinned BUILD revision/fingerprint and verified author/reviewer provenance. Operation identity binds run+subject+checkpoint+canonical target; timestamps and model usage are descriptive metadata and cannot create a second logical publication. sc4 owns durable intent acceptance and checkpoint freeze in its runtime namespace; staged-but-unaccepted intent is not authority. Accepted intent cardinality per run is zero or one; it references exactly one immutable coverage snapshot and canonical target revision, while distinct legitimate review runs may create later canonical CR revisions through existing lifecycle rules. One coverage snapshot retains the sc2 ledger, basis and trusted receipt references; runtime data stays out of artifact JSON. Artifact JSON carries compact investigation linkage only. [c1,c2,c4]

Proposed new file: src/workflow/code-review/investigation/completion-artifact.ts adapts accepted findings to existing DimensionResult and CodeReviewArtifact, preserving criterion/dimension order, severity, confidence, expectation/evidence identities and all findings. Reuse or extract existing runner fold/build/validate helpers without invoking runCodeReview's judge execution. Add optional body.investigation metadata with version, operationId, runId, subjectDigest, policyDigest, checkpointDigest, coverageRef and coverageDigest; old records omit it and remain readable. Keep existing reviewedBy party, BUILD fingerprint and canonical lifecycle content identity. Findings map into their pinned criteria; unknown criterion or unmappable location is a conflict, never silently discarded. Prefer evidence source path/range as finding location and retain structured evidence/expectation refs in additive metadata. Preserve current severity fold exactly: any HIGH block, else MED warn, else pass; confidence remains explicit and existing human approval policy is unchanged. Extend CodeReviewBody.groundingMode with the explicit value investigation for both new-engine modes, and add investigation.sourceMode (source-only or indexed-impact). Do not label new source-only runs degraded or new indexed runs graph-full: legacy full/degraded semantics and warn cap remain unchanged for legacy records. The new investigation mode uses the existing severity fold without a source-mode verdict floor; optional caller discovery is the only mode difference. Update canonical validators, rendering and completion-evidence readers to recognize the versioned mode; enum-strict older readers require s6 capability gating and are not claimed automatically compatible. Unsupported new-mode readers refuse rather than reinterpret the record. [c2,c3,c4]

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed new file: src/workflow/code-review/investigation/completion-publisher.ts consumes the sc4 publication fence and existing ArtifactStore/History/LifecycleService instance owned by the daemon. Build one immutable candidate and coverage snapshot; assess; accept frozen intent through sc4; then under its owner fence enter the canonical artifact queue. Use ArtifactStore.updateAndLog (or lifecycle-equivalent guarded content mutation) to compare current head revision/absence against frozen expected revision, and recheck scope/freshness/party/current owner immediately before mutation. Same operationId plus exact subject/checkpoint/content digest returns existing canonical revision without write. Any mismatching current record/revision is conflict; never overwrite to hide another run or a human-edited record. A lifecycle write and a run journal receipt are two recoverable commits, not one atomic cross-store transaction. After canonical write read back and validate the exact persisted head, then stage immutable ReviewCompletionReceiptV1 and call sc4.recordCompletion. On lost ACK, reconcile by frozen operation identity and canonical content/history; if canonical head has moved incompatibly, report conflict rather than regenerate. Rendered CR document is a regenerable canonical view, never the authority for success; temporary review reports remain /tmp. No direct filesystem artifact overwrite and no automatic approval/tracker message. [c2,c4]

The current sc4 implementation rejects lease claims for completion-requested state and has no accepted publication-intent binding. This is owned by s4, not s5. Before s5 PLAN/build, approve and implement the localized sc4-owned HLD amendment: expose an owner-fenced publication operation which durably binds exactly one intentRef and expected checkpoint, freezes further progress, permits restart/takeover while preserving frozen intent, and supplies a current-owner assertion inside the canonical commit callback. Same intent replay is idempotent; changed intent is conflict; a cancelled/stale/completed run cannot acquire new publication authority. Its critical section pins generation against concurrent takeover for a bounded canonical write, with freshness/owner checks immediately before CAS; journal receipt after write stays separately recoverable. sc5 consumes that capability and must not implement sc4 reducer/lease changes as its own task. Open question oq1 blocks PLAN until prerequisite ownership and approval are resolved. [c1,c4] Formal pending proposal: .insrc/artifacts/AMD-c32aa60534232f36-1.json. This is a prerequisite amendment request, not an implemented capability.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Own exact assessment/receipt types, accountable completion checks and canonical CR adapter/publisher; no model judging or autoapproval.
Revalidate exact selected packets, frozen context and approved contract/BUILD pins at assessment and canonical CAS; no generic HEAD diff.
Use validated ledger universe and trusted provenance; do not weaken evidence, findings or applicability rules.
A request-completion reply is a trigger only. All final findings/deltas must already be block-checkpoint accepted; no new final reply coverage accepted here.
Use replay, lease/fence, frozen publication intent and terminal receipt. Explicit prerequisite back-flow for missing capability; do not privately implement or forge its state events.
Stage immutable intent/coverage/receipt values through existing runtime ports. Usage observation quality/pending status preserved without making usage availability a false proof of review coverage.

errorCases.scenario: Required coverage/evidence or selected block assessment missing.
errorCases.detection: Revalidate ledger and enumerate required rows, latest block dispositions and outstanding work against pinned basis.
errorCases.response: Return incomplete with unresolved row IDs/reasons; no canonical CR or terminal success.

errorCases.detection: Compare trusted contract-decision conflicts and canonical authorPartyOf against authenticated reviewer party; refuse unknown/same party.
errorCases.response: Return conflict for human decision; never silently weaken approved requirements or label same-party result independent.
errorCases.userImpact: Human resolves conflicting requirements or chooses independent reviewer.

errorCases.detection: assertReviewSubjectFresh plus exact BUILD fingerprint/revision, policy/tool compatibility check at assessment and inside canonical CAS.
errorCases.response: Return stale without publishing for the new revision; preserve accepted evidence for diagnosis.
errorCases.userImpact: Further review required for changed scope.

errorCases.scenario: Crash or lost ACK between intent, canonical write and terminal receipt.
errorCases.detection: Read frozen sc4 intent, terminal receipt and canonical operationId/content digest under owner fence.
errorCases.response: Reconcile the same canonical revision; if absent apply expected-revision CAS once; if conflicting preserve conflict. No model rerun or new logical publication.
errorCases.userImpact: Resume publication without paying for accepted reasoning again.

errorCases.scenario: Concurrent completion or canonical CR changed by another run/person.
errorCases.detection: sc4 generation fence and ArtifactStore queue compare expected prior revision plus frozen operation identity.
errorCases.response: Identical operation returns original receipt; mismatching head or intent returns conflict, no overwrite.
errorCases.userImpact: No silent loss of newer review or human edits.

errorCases.scenario: Missing sc4 prerequisite or unsupported canonical reader capability.
errorCases.detection: Check frozen-intent/publication-fence support and versioned investigation metadata/grounding support before admission.
errorCases.response: Explicit unsupported/conflict; do not implement private sc4 events or pretend legacy records prove new coverage.
errorCases.userImpact: Prerequisite must be approved and delivered before s5 build/rollout.

errorCases.scenario: Canonical JSON succeeds but rendered document fails.
errorCases.detection: Verified head and operation identity exist while deterministic render reports IO failure.
errorCases.response: Retain canonical identity and regenerate document idempotently; report rendering limitation, never publish duplicate revision.
errorCases.userImpact: Review result survives; view repair pending.

migration.stateBefore: Discovery c1: sc4 persists accepted block state and simple completion-requested/completed transitions but cannot yet recover the frozen publication intent. Discovery c2: canonical runner executes judges then uses lifecycle-backed persistence, with legacy full/degraded labels and severity fold.
migration.stateAfter: sc5 assessment and versioned canonical adapter consume accepted coverage and an sc4-owned frozen-publication boundary. New engine remains unselected until s6 qualifies readers and transports; existing reviews retain behavior.

migrationSteps.action: Resolve oq1 and approve the localized sc4 amendment; deliver its recovery prerequisite under sc4 ownership before s5 PLAN/build. No s5 private recovery event implementation.

Add sc5 assessment/receipt types and pure validation plus versioned investigation metadata and explicit investigation grounding mode to canonical CR readers/validators. Existing full/degraded records retain original semantics.

Add canonical expected-revision publication adapter using the daemon's existing lifecycle instance and sc4 fence; verify deterministic crash/CAS/mode/approval fixtures without activating production engine.

s6 enables only after all consumers support the new canonical mode/version. Rollback routing preserves canonical records/history and frozen intents; older binaries must refuse unsupported new-mode publication rather than rewrite it as a legacy review.

migration.backwardCompat: Existing CR fields, verdict vocabulary, party and human override semantics preserved. New investigation records add compact versioned linkage and require an explicit canonical groundingMode extension for equal source/index verdict treatment; older enum-strict readers are NOT automatically compatible. Reader validation/rendering changes are scoped to canonical CR and must be capability-gated by s6. No conversion of legacy partial logs into resumable coverage, no default routing change or artifact backfill.

alternativesConsidered.name: Frozen completion intent and canonical compare-and-set
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Assess accepted coverage, freeze one publication intent, and reconcile canonical CR by deterministic identity.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use sc2/sc4 replay for deterministic assessment, stage immutable coverage and candidate CR, persist an owner-fenced sc4 publication intent, then write through the existing ArtifactStore queue with expected-revision and operation-identity checks. Complete sc4 receipt only after verifying canonical content. A restart reuses the same frozen intent and canonical revision rather than running judges again. Requires a localized sc4 recovery prerequisite; s5 consumes it, never writes private sc4 events.
pros: Smallest design preserving accepted work and existing canonical lifecycle.
Lost artifact-write or terminal-receipt ACK is reconciled by identity rather than republishing.
cons: Requires explicit sc4 back-flow for completion-requested takeover and frozen intent/fenced publication boundary.
Two stores require a recoverable intent protocol rather than pretending to share an atomic transaction.

alternativesConsidered.name: Durable canonical publication outbox
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Queue frozen completion payloads for a separate daemon publication worker.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Perform the same coverage/freshness/party assessment and store a frozen sc4 intent, then hand it to a dedicated worker which serially applies canonical artifact CAS and records receipt. Worker revalidates freshness and ownership before writes, with the same sc4 recovery prerequisite.
pros: Separates publication scheduling from reviewer lifetime.
Explicit retry queue for transient storage failures.
cons: Adds a new scheduler and worker lifecycle without a Story requirement.
Still needs frozen intent, generation fencing and canonical idempotency; does not remove the hard boundary.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Dedicated publication worker unnecessary for one bounded canonical write and still requires the same recovery protocol.
